[{:db/id "59b59f9f-0328-5e3a-b3a0-9ae94cd9029b" :answer/id #uuid "59b59f9f-0328-5e3a-b3a0-9ae94cd9029b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "9\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "8ed0441f-d7c8-59ac-b964-78a874544707" :answer/id #uuid "8ed0441f-d7c8-59ac-b964-78a874544707" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "13\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "b6c8bae0-5d37-5021-8cbd-592d9fbcffea" :answer/id #uuid "b6c8bae0-5d37-5021-8cbd-592d9fbcffea" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "6\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "c9905343-f98e-5172-a713-e8ad676df9ec" :answer/id #uuid "c9905343-f98e-5172-a713-e8ad676df9ec" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "26\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "6cc12c7b-7d04-5703-959a-c62329b886f5" :answer/id #uuid "6cc12c7b-7d04-5703-959a-c62329b886f5" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "11\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "56bac0d5-d078-5477-b2fe-4ca3e2469c85" :answer-field/id #uuid "56bac0d5-d078-5477-b2fe-4ca3e2469c85" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/choices ["59b59f9f-0328-5e3a-b3a0-9ae94cd9029b" "8ed0441f-d7c8-59ac-b964-78a874544707" "b6c8bae0-5d37-5021-8cbd-592d9fbcffea" "c9905343-f98e-5172-a713-e8ad676df9ec" "6cc12c7b-7d04-5703-959a-c62329b886f5"] :answer-field/correct "8ed0441f-d7c8-59ac-b964-78a874544707" :db/ensure :answer-field/validate} {:db/id "7bca55c5-9e2a-5abf-bde2-2e93390e2953" :question/id #uuid "7bca55c5-9e2a-5abf-bde2-2e93390e2953" :question/problem "Simon measures the temperature of the tea in his cup, and the thermometer displays a reading of ${59}^{∘}C.$ After $2$ minutes, Simon repeats the measurement and the thermometer displays a reading of  ${51}^{∘}C.$ To the nearest minute, how long does it take for the tea to decrease its temperature to ${26}^{∘}C$ if the temperature in the room is ${12}^{∘}C?$ 

*Hint: You may assume that the temperature $T(t)$ of the tea in Simon's cup decreases at a rate that obeys Newton's law of cooling, where $T$ is measured in degrees Celsius and $t>0$ is the time, in minutes, since the first measurement.*" :question/worked-solution "Newton's law of cooling states that the rate at which the temperature $T(t)$ of a body changes is proportional to the difference between its temperature and its surroundings. Therefore, we have the inhibited decay equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}=-k(T-{T}_{S}),
$$

where ${T}_{S}$ is the temperature of the surroundings, and $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.

In our case, ${T}_{S}={12}^{∘}\text{C},$ and we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}=-k(T-12).
$$

First, we integrate our differential equation by separating the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dT}{T-12} & =-k\,dt \\ \int \frac{dT}{T-12} & =-k\int dt \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|T-12| & =-kt+C\end{aligned}
$$

Since this is the solution to an inhibited decay equation, we have $T-12>0$ for all $t>0.$
Next, we solve for $T(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T-12 & ={e}^{-kt+C} \\ T-12 & ={e}^{C}{e}^{-kt} \\ T-12 & =K{e}^{-kt} \\ T & =12+K{e}^{-kt}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $K={e}^{C}$ is a constant of integration. 

We're told that the initial temperature reading was ${59}^{∘}C.$ So, we apply the initial condition $T(0)=59,$ and solve for $K:$

$$
\begin{aligned}59 & =12+K{e}^{0} \\ 59 & =12+K \\ K & =47\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following expression for $T(t):$

$$
T(t)=12+47{e}^{-kt}
$$

We're also told that, after $2$ minutes, the thermometer reading is ${51}^{∘}C.$ So, applying the condition $T(2)=51,$ we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}51 & =12+47{e}^{-2k} \\ 39 & =47{e}^{-2k} \\ \frac{39}{47} & ={e}^{-2k} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{39}{47}) & =-2k \\ k & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{39}{47})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the temperature of the tea is ${26}^{∘}C.$ Then, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T({t}_{1}) & =26 \\ 12+47{e}^{-k{t}_{1}} & =26 \\ 47{e}^{-k{t}_{1}} & =14 \\ {e}^{-k{t}_{1}} & =\frac{14}{47} \\ -k{t}_{1} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{14}{47}) \\ {t}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{k}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{14}{47}).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting in our value for $k,$ we conclude that the tea will have a temperature of ${26}^{∘}C$ after

$$
{t}_{1}=\frac{-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{14}{47})}{-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{39}{47})}≈13\,\text{min},
$$

rounded to the nearest minute." :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["56bac0d5-d078-5477-b2fe-4ca3e2469c85"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "42a5f854-c421-5906-9531-dfb338eb3d00" :answer/id #uuid "42a5f854-c421-5906-9531-dfb338eb3d00" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "8\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "68bd5f21-2fc4-57db-ab21-cd5920a10ff8" :answer/id #uuid "68bd5f21-2fc4-57db-ab21-cd5920a10ff8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "14\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "b750d51c-f2a0-5a6c-a1e6-ddae4ed1f957" :answer/id #uuid "b750d51c-f2a0-5a6c-a1e6-ddae4ed1f957" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "11\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "14340294-f6e6-5843-a6fe-4ec754aa2b3a" :answer/id #uuid "14340294-f6e6-5843-a6fe-4ec754aa2b3a" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "15\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "26c1b56e-8363-5b7a-9cd7-fc35a89b4352" :answer/id #uuid "26c1b56e-8363-5b7a-9cd7-fc35a89b4352" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "30\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "773705ba-e6bc-585e-ac23-61ef9313aea0" :answer-field/id #uuid "773705ba-e6bc-585e-ac23-61ef9313aea0" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/choices ["42a5f854-c421-5906-9531-dfb338eb3d00" "68bd5f21-2fc4-57db-ab21-cd5920a10ff8" "b750d51c-f2a0-5a6c-a1e6-ddae4ed1f957" "14340294-f6e6-5843-a6fe-4ec754aa2b3a" "26c1b56e-8363-5b7a-9cd7-fc35a89b4352"] :answer-field/correct "14340294-f6e6-5843-a6fe-4ec754aa2b3a" :db/ensure :answer-field/validate} {:db/id "83a0fd6e-0040-59af-810e-aa17184cf1d7" :question/id #uuid "83a0fd6e-0040-59af-810e-aa17184cf1d7" :question/problem "The water boils in a pan at a temperature of ${100}^{∘}C.$ The pan with water is then placed to a room with a temperature of ${17}^{∘}C,$ and the temperature of water decreases. To the nearest minute, how long after cooling began does the body reach ${19}^{∘}\text{C}$?" :question/worked-solution "Newton's law of cooling states that the rate at which the temperature $T(t)$ of a body changes is proportional to the difference between its temperature and its surroundings. Therefore, we have the inhibited decay equation

$$
\frac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-12),\qquad k>0.
$$

First, we integrate our differential equation by separating the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dT}{T-12} & =-k\,dt \\ \int \frac{dT}{T-12} & =-k\int dt \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|T-12| & =-kt+C\end{aligned}
$$

Since this is the solution to an inhibited decay equation, we have $T-12>0$ for all $t>0.$
Next, we solve for $T(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T-12 & ={e}^{-kt+C} \\ T-12 & ={e}^{C}{e}^{-kt} \\ T-12 & =K{e}^{-kt} \\ T & =12+K{e}^{-kt}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $K={e}^{C}$ is a constant of integration. 

Apply the two observed conditions $T(1)=64$ and $T(4)=49$:

$$
\begin{aligned}64 & =12+Ke^{-1k} \\ 52 & =Ke^{-1k} \\ 49 & =12+Ke^{-4k} \\ 37 & =Ke^{-4k}\end{aligned}
$$

Divide the excess temperatures to eliminate $K$, then take natural logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{37}{52} & =\frac{Ke^{-4k}}{Ke^{-1k}} \\ \frac{37}{52} & =e^{-3k} \\ \ln(\frac{37}{52}) & =-3k \\ k & =- \frac{\ln{\left(\frac{37}{52} \right)}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute this rate into $T(1)=64$ to determine the constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}52 & =Ke^{-1(- \frac{\ln{\left(\frac{37}{52} \right)}}{3})} \\ K & =52e^{1(- \frac{\ln{\left(\frac{37}{52} \right)}}{3})} \\ K & =52\left(\frac{52}{37}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution satisfying both observations is

$$
T(t)=12+52\left(\frac{52}{37}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}e^{-(- \frac{\ln{\left(\frac{37}{52} \right)}}{3})t}.
$$

Substituting the two observation times confirms the model:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1) & =12+(52\left(\frac{52}{37}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}})e^{-(- \frac{\ln{\left(\frac{37}{52} \right)}}{3})\cdot 1}=64 \\ T(4) & =12+(52\left(\frac{52}{37}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}})e^{-(- \frac{\ln{\left(\frac{37}{52} \right)}}{3})\cdot 4}=49\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the body reaches ${19}^{∘}\text{C}.$ Then, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T({t}_{1}) & =19 \\ 12+Ke^{-k{t}_{1}} & =19 \\ Ke^{-k{t}_{1}} & =7 \\ e^{-k{t}_{1}} & =\frac{7}{K} \\ -k{t}_{1} & =\ln\left(\frac{7}{K}\right) \\ {t}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{k}\ln\left(\frac{7}{K}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the values of $K$ and $k$ to obtain the time measured since cooling began:

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{- \frac{\ln{\left(\frac{37}{52} \right)}}{3}}\ln\left(\frac{7}{52\left(\frac{52}{37}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}}\right) \\ {t}_{1} & =1+3\frac{\ln(\frac{7}{52})}{\ln(\frac{37}{52})}≈19\,\text{min}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["ab2a34ec-9222-55be-9af3-842e7b4fe46d"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "64fd9fd9-a113-5826-9e9f-9bf1153c8645" :answer/id #uuid "64fd9fd9-a113-5826-9e9f-9bf1153c8645" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "19\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "108ed220-ff0d-5a3e-9732-871db25e264d" :answer/id #uuid "108ed220-ff0d-5a3e-9732-871db25e264d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "42\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "751594c1-eba1-5f1c-a604-af02b2e24eff" :answer/id #uuid "751594c1-eba1-5f1c-a604-af02b2e24eff" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "12\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "36b98352-a45c-5756-ba26-e8f13b324484" :answer/id #uuid "36b98352-a45c-5756-ba26-e8f13b324484" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "22\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "40afc4ac-32fd-5122-8320-a1b94bc430b1" :answer/id #uuid "40afc4ac-32fd-5122-8320-a1b94bc430b1" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "20\,\text{min}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "f54cefd1-735e-592f-a832-09bdfef2567e" :answer-field/id #uuid "f54cefd1-735e-592f-a832-09bdfef2567e" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/choices ["64fd9fd9-a113-5826-9e9f-9bf1153c8645" "108ed220-ff0d-5a3e-9732-871db25e264d" "751594c1-eba1-5f1c-a604-af02b2e24eff" "36b98352-a45c-5756-ba26-e8f13b324484" "40afc4ac-32fd-5122-8320-a1b94bc430b1"] :answer-field/correct "36b98352-a45c-5756-ba26-e8f13b324484" :db/ensure :answer-field/validate} {:db/id "6178d66f-8125-5a9f-a46c-197579fd4dfe" :question/id #uuid "6178d66f-8125-5a9f-a46c-197579fd4dfe" :question/problem "A heated metal body cools in a room at ${14}^{∘}\text{C}.$ Its temperature is ${114}^{∘}\text{C}$ after $2$ minutes and ${79}^{∘}\text{C}$ after $7$ minutes.
